newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries steady in Tokyo, await data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries steady in Tokyo, await data.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were little changed by midday Tokyo, with the market largely focusing on a slew of key U.S. economic data to be released this week, including Employment Cost Index (ECI) data due on Tuesday, traders said.
Some profit-taking interest was detected on the topside, while losses were limited as buying-on-dips demand continues to persist, a trader at a Japanese bank said.
"We have many economic indicators this week. Some traders with long positions are taking profits on the topside, but there is buying on dips as well," he said.

In addition to the ECI data, an important gauge of inflationary pressure, the market will also focus on non-farm payroll and the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) reports for July, due on Friday.

"Personally, I believe that the economic data this week will remain in line with market expectations... If the economic indicators suggest there isn't going to be a rise in U.S. interest rates this year, then the market will be watching closely to see how much Treasuries rally further," the trader said, adding the next target for the yield of the key 30-year bond will be 6.375 percent and then 6.25 percent.
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond was at 102-07/32 at 0305 GMT, yielding 6.46 percent, unchanged from Friday's close.
Meanwhile, the September T-bond futures contract was down 4/32 at 114-29/32, compared with 115-1/32 at the previous close.
